History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
53-year-old man with one-week history of painless but warm swelling over the left olecranon; video exam consistent with olecranon bursitis. NSAID therapy started and blood work ordered to exclude infection, gout, or other inflammatory causes.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Localized swelling over the back (olecranon) of the left elbow noticed ~1 week ago while showering.  
• Characteristics: Swelling feels “a bit warm”; minimally tender adjacent to the tip; no significant pain; full range of motion maintained.  
• Course/progression: Unchanged over the past week; no prior episodes.  
• Aggravating/relieving factors: None identified; no recalled trauma or repetitive pressure.  
• Associated symptoms: Denies systemic symptoms (fever, malaise), no redness reported, no other joint involvement.  
• Review of systems: Negative for skin rash/eczema except mild dryness over elbow; denies other dermatologic or rheumatologic symptoms.

Past Medical History:
• Osteoarthritis – primary-care diagnosis several years ago (details not discussed).  
• Peanut allergy – IgE-mediated reaction per patient.  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• No regular medications.  
• Ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food – newly recommended (dose/route/frequency documented).  
Allergies: Peanuts (food). No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Occupation: Desk job.  
• Exercise: Runs 2–3 times/week.  
• Tobacco/alcohol/substance use: Not discussed.  
• Living/financial issues: Not discussed.

Family History:
• No known family history of rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, or other rheumatologic conditions.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded.  
• General: Appears well on video.  
• Left elbow: Visible soft swelling over olecranon; overlying skin slightly warm and dry; minimal tenderness adjacent to tip; full active range of motion; no pronounced erythema noted.  
• Other systems: Not examined/recorded.

Investigations:
• To be arranged: Blood panel including CBC, inflammatory markers (e.g., ESR/CRP), rheumatologic antibodies, and serum urate. Results expected ~5–6 days after sampling.

Assessment & Plan:

Overall Impression:
Likely aseptic (non-infectious) olecranon bursitis of the left elbow; infection, gout, and systemic inflammatory disease to be excluded with labs.

DDx Integration:
1. Aseptic olecranon bursitis – painless swelling, slight warmth, preserved function.  
2. Septic olecranon bursitis – considered due to warmth; less likely given minimal tenderness and no systemic signs.  
3. Gouty bursitis – possible; male >50 yrs, testing planned; no prior gout history.

Issue 1: Left olecranon bursitis  
• Assessment: Presentation most consistent with aseptic inflammation of the bursa.  
• Plan:  
  – Start NSAID: Ibuprofen 400 mg PO BID with food; stop if GI symptoms.  
  – Relative rest; avoid direct pressure on elbow.  
  – Arrange blood tests (CBC, ESR/CRP, rheumatoid panel, urate) – forms mailed to patient.  
  – Re-evaluate via phone/video or in-person once results available (~1 week).  
  – Red-flag advice: Seek urgent care if elbow becomes markedly red, increasingly painful, or if systemic symptoms (fever, chills) develop—concern for septic arthritis/bursitis.

Issue 2: Rule-out infectious or crystalline etiology  
• Assessment: Need to exclude septic bursitis and gout.  
• Plan:  
  – Perform above laboratory screen.  
  – Consider aspiration for Gram stain/culture if clinical worsening or lab markers raised (to be decided at follow-up).

Issue 3: Background osteoarthritis  
• Assessment: Historical diagnosis, currently asymptomatic in elbow.  
• Plan: No immediate intervention; will revisit if joint symptoms emerge during follow-up.

General plan items:  
• Follow-up appointment to review blood results and clinical course (patient to book once tests completed).  
• Provide written after-care instructions and contact information for urgent concerns.

Quality checks:
● Missing vitals (BP, HR, Temp) – not obtainable via current video consult.  
● Medication list limited to newly prescribed NSAID; full reconciliation advisable at next visit.  
● Social history incomplete (tobacco/alcohol).  
● No documented family history beyond rheumatologic enquiry.  
● Transcript quality adequate; minor inaudible gaps did not affect clinical content.
